career_ladder.note: Judicial officers in Kerala are appointed under the Kerala Judicial Service Rules, 1991 under the superintendence and administrative control of the High Court of Kerala. Pay scales follow the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) revised pay matrix for the Subordinate Judiciary, with advancement based on seniority-cum-merit and suitability evaluations.

exam_scheme.note: Selection process conducted directly by the High Court of Kerala consists of three successive stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective screening of 100 questions carrying 200 marks), Main Written Examination (4 descriptive papers of 100 marks each, 3 hours duration each), followed by a Viva-Voce test (50 marks). Final merit list is determined by the aggregate marks obtained in the Main Written Examination and Viva-Voce (total 450 marks).

stages.source_label: High Court of Kerala Kerala Judicial Service Examination Notification & Scheme

papers.paper_name: Part A: Civil Laws (CPC, Indian Contract Act, Negotiable Instruments Act, Transfer of Property Act, Specific Relief Act, Kerala Building Lease and Rent Control Act)
papers.qualifying_threshold: 40% (80/200) for General/OBC; 35% (70/200) for SC/ST; shortlisted for Mains in a 1:10 ratio of notified vacancies

papers.paper_name: Part B: Criminal Laws (CrPC, Indian Penal Code, Indian Evidence Act)
Part C: Constitution of India, Legal General Knowledge, Reasoning and Mental Ability

stages.source_label: High Court of Kerala Munsiff-Magistrate Written Examination Regulations

papers.paper_name: Paper I: English Essay, Translation (English to Malayalam & Malayalam to English), Precis Writing and Legal Notes
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each paper and 45% aggregate (35% in each paper and 40% aggregate for SC/ST)

papers.paper_name: Paper II: Civil Laws (Indian Contract Act, Transfer of Property Act, Limitation Act, Specific Relief Act, Easements Act, Kerala Building Lease & Rent Control Act, Hindu Succession Act, Indian Succession Act, Kerala Land Reforms Act)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each paper and 45% aggregate (35% in each paper and 40% aggregate for SC/ST)

papers.paper_name: Paper III: Criminal Laws (Indian Penal Code, Criminal Procedure Code, Indian Evidence Act)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each paper and 45% aggregate (35% in each paper and 40% aggregate for SC/ST)

papers.paper_name: Paper IV: Civil Rules of Practice, Kerala Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, Kerala Stamp Act, Criminal Rules of Practice, Framing of Charges and Judgment Writing
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each paper and 45% aggregate (35% in each paper and 40% aggregate for SC/ST)

stages.source_label: Kerala Judicial Service Rules, 1991 (Viva-Voce Evaluation Clause)

papers.paper_name: Oral Interview & Comprehensive Legal Personality Assessment
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% (20 marks out of 50) for General/OBC; 35% (17.5 marks out of 50) for SC/ST candidates

financial_package.note: Salary computed as per the Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) revised pay matrix for the Subordinate Judiciary (Level J-1: ₹77,840–₹1,36,520; Entry Basic Pay ₹77,840) as accepted by the Government of Kerala pursuant to Supreme Court directives. Applies standardized project constant 58% DA as of 2025-07-01.
financial_package.pay_source_label: Second National Judicial Pay Commission (SNJPC) Recommendation Matrix and Government of Kerala Implementation Order
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated with Entry Basic Pay of ₹77,840 at mandatory 58% DA (₹45,147) plus Judicial HRA / designated government judicial quarters, sumptuary allowance (₹4,000), robe allowance, conveyance allowance, and electricity/water reimbursement, less statutory pension and income tax deductions.
official_perks: Designated judicial bungalow / official residence or judicial HRA
Official vehicle / conveyance allowance with driver
Sumptuary allowance, library allowance, and book grant as per SNJPC
Free electricity and water quota as prescribed under judicial service rules
Comprehensive medical cover for officer and family dependents under judicial regulations
Robe allowance and telephone / broadband reimbursement
